steps.message:
# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same regular file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded without touching whatever they point to.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

### Summary of Changes

The [`TextFileBasedViolationStore`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java) was updated to maintain the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and violation files according to the configured integrity mode:

1. **Integrity Mode Configuration (`default.integrity`)**:
   - Added configuration property `default.integrity` with possible values `repair` and `ignore` (defaulting to `ignore`).
   - When set to `repair`, the store inspects the index (`stored.rules`) and folder as they exist on disk during `initialize(...)`, reloading the latest state from disk even if the folder was previously initialized.
   - When defaulting to or set to `ignore`, no integrity checks or repairs are performed.

2. **Entry Classification**:
   - **Shared**: Entries pointing to the same file name (even if the file does not exist) or pointing to the same regular file (via hard links, symbolic links, or directly, even if pointing outside the store folder) are identified as shared. If an entry is shared, it remains shared regardless of other conditions. Shared entries and files that no entry points to are never touched during repair.
   - **Broken**: An entry is broken if its file name is not a valid path or points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the store folder (e.g. non-existent files, directories, subdirectories, parent directory traversals, dangling symlinks, or symlinks to directories). When `repair` is enabled, broken entries are discarded from `stored.rules` without touching whatever they point to.
   - **Resolved**: An entry that is not broken and has no violations (including files that are empty or contain only line breaks) is considered resolved. When `repair` is enabled, resolved entries are removed from `stored.rules`, and their violation files are deleted. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link, both the link and the target file it points to are deleted.

3. **Rule Forgetting on Save with `repair`**:
   - Saving no violations (`violations.isEmpty()`) for an unknown rule saves nothing (no new file or index entry created).
   - Saving no violations for a known rule forgets the rule: removes its entry from `stored.rules` and deletes its file (including both the symlink and target file if it points to a symbolic link, even outside the store folder).
   - If another entry is sharing that file, only the entry is removed from `stored.rules`, leaving the shared file untouched.
   - If deleting the file fails (e.g. permission error), saving fails by throwing [`StoreUpdateFailedException`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/StoreUpdateFailedException.java) and leaves the entry in `stored.rules`.

### Verification

All changes were verified using Gradle:
- **Unit and Integration Tests**: Added comprehensive test cases in [`TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest.java) covering:
  - Default `ignore` mode behavior.
  - Broken entry discard across missing files, directories, subdirectories, invalid path names, and dangling symlinks.
  - Resolved entry discard and deletion of files with 0 violations and only line breaks.
  - Symlink deletion of both the link in the store folder and target files outside the folder.
  - Preservation of shared entries across identical names, hard links, and symlinks to files outside the folder.
  - Preservation of unreferenced (orphan) files in the store directory.
  - Verification that initialization in `repair` mode inspects disk even after prior initialization of the same folder.
